summary:
Well, well, well... Week 6 gave us the kind of scoring spread that makes you wonder if half the league forgot they were playing football. We had cosmohouck dropping 164.88 points like he's playing a different sport, while TophTT limped in with 43.36—which, coincidentally, is also the number of excuses he's preparing for next week's group chat.

Let's talk about the battle of the titans that wasn't: mjgrana versus cosmohouck. These are your #2 and #1 power-ranked teams, and they delivered a combined 316.12 points. *En fuego!* Bijan Robinson put up 32.8 for cosmohouck while Drake Maye added 27.2—you can't stop them, you can only hope to contain them. Meanwhile, mjgrana's George Pickens dropped 27.3 and still lost by 13.64. That's what we call "bringing a knife to a gunfight," except the knife was pretty sharp and the gun just happened to be a bazooka. But here's the thing about starting Matthew Stafford when he gives you 9.3 points: sometimes you win *despite* your decisions, not because of them.

Then we have "The Donut King" TophTT, who somehow managed to start two tight ends—Ja'Tavion Sanders and Dalton Kincaid—who combined for a magnificent zero points. Not zero *touchdowns*, mind you. Zero *points*. That's actually impressive in its own tragic way. You can't stop him from rostering goose eggs, you can only hope to contain your laughter. Kenneth Gainwell led his team with 6.6 points, which tells you everything you need to know about how this 43.36-point masterpiece came together. I've seen better production from a vending machine that only accepts Canadian quarters.

And let's give a slow clap to "Rico Suave" Langland, who got 31.9 points from Rico Dowdle and still lost by 34.04 points. That's like hitting a home run in the first inning and then watching your team give up 15 runs. Calvin Ridley's 2.3 points and Keon Coleman's 2.6 weren't just bad—they were "maybe I should've checked if they were actually playing this week" bad. Meanwhile, Shogunation's Drake London went *en fuego* with 26.8 points, proving once again that sometimes it's better to be lucky than good... though in this matchup, you didn't really need to be either.

Week 6: Where the rich got richer, the poor got poorer, and TophTT's tight ends got absolutely nothing. You can't stop fantasy football from being cruel, you can only hope to contain the damage to your pride.
